result:
Audit of p1, round 1. I assumed the submission was wrong and went looking; most of it holds up, one claim in the delivered document does not.

## What I verified independently

**R7 / ground truth.** Read `page_002.txt` and `page_002.png` myself plus `ingest/manifest.json` (`figures: []`, the one image per page is the ND monogram in the header — visible in the render). The brief's transcription is verbatim correct, notebook cells 12–19 match, Q3 is correctly absent. `hasattr(torch_geometric.utils, "segment_attention")` is `False` in PyG 2.8.1 — the handout defect the answer notes is real. `gt_framework.py` is byte-identical to `shared/`.

**Correctness, by my own suite** (`validators/p1/work/val_check.py`, log `validators/p1/logs/val_check.log`), not reusing the worker's helpers: `hop_distances` against `scipy.sparse.csgraph.shortest_path` on 30 ZINC graphs, a hand-built disconnected graph with an isolated node, caps 1/3/8, and 12 LastFM sources — exact everywhere, unreachable stays −1 under a cap; eigenvectors by Rayleigh quotient against the dense spectrum, orthonormal, orthogonal to D^{1/2}**1**, zero-padded correctly; `attention_pairs` set-equal to {d(i,j) ≤ 2} ∪ virtual on 20 graphs; the **sparse** forward against a hand-built dense reference on the real (non-complete) pair set — 1.19e-07; the dense forward — 0.0; `enc["spd"] == D[querier, attended]` for every pair; pair counts 189.1828/graph and 804,349 on LastFM. All pass. The worker's own 26 checks also re-run clean in my directory.

**Provenance.** Every table cell and every prose number traces to a JSON log; the three listings are byte-verbatim from `solution.py`. LaTeX compiles clean in a minimal wrapper (6 pages, 0 overfull boxes), labels and the `p1py`/`p1kw`/`p1cm`/`p1st` names all namespaced, `lint_output.py` OK, `downloads.md` consistent.

**My own reruns** (`logs/val_rerun.log`): cell 18 → val 0.4451/0.4418, test 0.4792/0.4766; `local+virtual` → 0.4770/0.4941; `local` → 0.4862/0.5036. The Q2 ranking survives.

## Defects

- **[1.1] major — the answer contradicts itself and the data.** The `SparseSPDAttention` docstring, printed verbatim in the Q2 listing, says the 2-hop ball "had the lowest validation MAE on ZINC **and the highest validation micro-F1 on LastFM**". `logs/lastfm_final_results.json`: `local` 0.8152, 2-hop ball 0.8100 — **second**, not highest. The answer's own prose two pages earlier says "the submitted set second of five". `switch_submitted.py` wrote that docstring against the pre-sign-flip-fix `lastfm_nodetask_results.json` (where 2-hop *was* highest at 0.6815) and nobody updated it after `run_lastfm_final.py` reordered the ranking. `build_answer.py`'s asserts (lines 254–262) guard the generated prose but not the spliced docstrings.
- **[1.2] minor — Table 2's bolded row (val 0.4293 / test 0.4677) has never been reproduced.** Six later runs all land worse: the worker's three (`logs/zinc_cell18.log`; `rerun_checks.log` literally says "DIFFERENT, investigate") and my two. The caption discloses the three *test* repeats — honest — but the val column, on which "picked on validation" rests, is printed as the single best draw with no such note.
- **[1.3] minor** — "the expander ... alone keeps the pair count O(n) while mixing in O(log n) hops": `local` and `local+virtual` are also O(n) pairs, and `local+virtual` mixes in 2 hops.
- **[1.4] minor** — "Two hops wins again, at 3 of the 3 seeds and by 0.0184 on the mean" mixes metrics; the counter is computed against `local+virtual` only, and on test MAE at seed 2 `local` (0.5073) beats the 2-hop ball (0.5098). True on validation MAE — say so.
- **[1.5] minor** — `\label{p1:tab:q2lastfm}` defined, never `\ref`'d.
- **[1.6] minor — R8.** My count (listings, table bodies, captions excluded): Q1 385, Q2 362, total 747 against ~300/question. Q1 is 28% over, just past the quarter threshold; no padding of the four kinds R8 names, so ~30 words off Q1 clears it. Table 2's caption is ~145 words.
- **[1.7] minor** — `submission.md` says "26 checks" where `notes.md` says "21/21", and "within 0.005 validation micro-F1" where the measured spread is 0.0079.

Checklist written to `validators/p1/checklist.md`. Only [1.1] is substantive — a one-line edit plus an assert — but a grader reading the listing is told something the measurements contradict, so it does not pass as-is.

VERDICT: FAIL
